summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease was admitted for persistent left knee pain and fatigue. Evaluation revealed a left peroneal vein deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary edema due to volume overload, and incidental lower lobe pneumonia. He was treated with anticoagulation (heparin bridged to warfarin), IV diuresis transitioned to oral torsemide, and a five-day course of antibiotics. His kidney function improved from a creatinine of 2.9 to 2.2, and his symptoms resolved. Irbesartan was held due to concerns for renal perfusion, amlodipine was increased for blood pressure control, and pantoprazole was doubled for GERD. He was discharged home on warfarin, updated antihypertensives, and instructions for close outpatient follow-up.
